docs.title: toffeeOS Development Version Documentation
docs.text: You might know this as toffeeOS, our in-house and currently secret OS environment for desktops built atop Linux. You might know that as GNU/Linux. We're making the documentation for the Development Version public to our testers and any interested parties who may be interested in how our OS works! Eventually, our OS will release as toffeeOS 1, and be free and open-source to all.

docs.title: Prerelease Testing Agreement
docs.text:
By testing prerelease software on devices not authorized by the dev teams through the minimum system requirements, you agree that you will be held responsible for all physical damage (corrupted storage, non-working peripherals, etc.) that may be inflicted upon your device.

This project (and its volunteers) will provide software support for all release channels on any device running toffeeOS or chocolateOS. We cannot provide hardware support, please speak with your vendor about that.

docs.title: Graphics API
docs.text:
As of toffeeOS Developer Version 1.6.2 (and later), the Vulkan Graphics API will be enabled by default on x86_64 (64-bit) systems, and OpenGL will be deprecated and disabled by default for these systems. It will still be available through other means, such as PPAs, our repos, etc., however.

In toffeeOS Developer Version 1.8, the Vulkan Graphics API will become the only API bundled and enabled by default. OpenGL will be removed from repos and PPAs. Should third-party repos include them, we may take action to warn the user that we cannot diagnose any issues regarding OpenGL (through a tip in the Terminal and/or pop-up in userspace) in the future but will not disallow installation.

In toffeeOS Developer Version 2.0, we began disallowing OpenGL access in API level 200 due to incompatibility with our rewrite.

docs.title: Changes to Release Channels
docs.text:
We're changing the names and purposes of our Release Channels effective September 2021. This brings clarity to our software development structure and better describes the channels and their purposes of existence.

Old Channel Name Old Channel Purpose New Channel Name New Channel Purpose Beta To test PreRel (pre-release) versions of the codename "toffeeOS Developer Version" operating system. Stable To test stable versions of the prerelease codename "toffeeOS Developer Version" operating system. Canary To test the next Beta versions of the codename "toffeeOS Developer Version" operating system. Beta To test PreRel (pre-release) versions of the codename "toffeeOS Developer Version" operating system. Dev To test the alpha builds "hot off the press" from our team of the codename "toffeeOS Developer Version" operating system. Alpha To test the alpha builds "hot off the press" from our team of the codename "toffeeOS Developer Version" operating system.

Users on the previous Beta channel will be automatically moved to the new Beta channel unless they choose to move to Stable in the software update pane (Any downgrades, should there be any required, are possible for these channels as they're currently testing the same release version.)

All users on the previous Canary and Dev channels will be opted in to the new Beta and Alpha channels respectively automatically with no prompt (Downgrades will not be possible for Alpha channel users.)

Despite the Stable branding, we have no plans to release a public beta at this time due to some instability with the current Stable release, toffeeOS Developer Version Development Version 1.5.

docs.title: OpenGL Support
docs.text:
OpenGL is natively supported and enabled by default in toffeeOS Developer Version 1.5 and earlier. OpenGL is supported but not enabled by default in toffeeOS Developer Version 1.6.1 and later.

For details, see the Graphics APIs doc.

docs.title: toffeeOS Developer Version (toffeeOS) system compatibility
docs.text:
Due to the upcoming x86 support deprecation, we recommend installing toffeeOS Developer Version on a 64-bit processor.

The requirements below are subject to change at any time.

docs.title: RAM
docs.text:
• Minimum: 4GB
  • Recommended: 16GB

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• CPU
  • Intel: Must be a 64-bit processor, released in 2014 or later.
  • AMD: Must be a 64-bit processor, Ryzen 1000 series or later only.
  • Apple: Must be a 64-bit processor, M1/M2 families only.
  • Discrete GPU (x86_64 on Intel/AMD 64-bit only): NVIDIA GPU launched in 2016 or later.
  • Specifics: GTX 1050 or later, GT cards are no longer supported by our team officially.
  • Discrete GPUs must support Vulkan 1.4 or later.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
• Minimum storage space needed for install: 15 GB
  • Recommended storage space (after install): 256+ GB SSD
  • Hard/Fusion/Hybrid Drives are NOT supported.

docs.title: RAM
docs.text:
• Minimum: 4GB
  • Recommended: 8GB

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• CPU: Intel CPU launched in 2013 or later; AMD A8 APUs released in 2014 and later, and Ryzen 1000 and later.
  • CPU and Motherboard (MBO) pairing must also support UEFI. CPU and MBO pairings without UEFI cannot boot the OS.
  • Intel processors from 2012 and earlier are no longer supported and will remain on toffeeOS Developer Version 1.5 non-LTS.
  • We do not support AMD CPUs prior to Ryzen 1000 or AMD APUs prior to 2014 A8 due to technical limitations.
  • GPU (64-bit only): NVIDIA GPU launched in 2014 or later.
  • Specifics: GT 705 or later, GTX 745 or later, and GTX Titan or later.
  • GPU must support Vulkan.

docs.title: Storage

  • Recommended storage space (after install): 320+ GB HDD/SSD
  • Fusion/Hybrid drives are NOT supported.

  • Maximum (32-bit only): 4GB
  • Recommended: 4GB (both)

docs.title: Android Apps on toffeeOS
docs.text:
Since we use APK files on frappeOS, and we have a mission to unify the "ecosystem," we've built in the ability to run Android apps on toffeeOS Developer Version natively.

To activate this feature (experimental), open our console app, and type either of following commands (depending on your version):

docs.title: toffeeOS Developer Version 2.0 and later
docs.text: sudo toffget toffee-apkrunner -y

docs.title: toffeeOS Developer Version 1.8 and earlier
docs.text:
Feature no longer supported, final version of these releases is 1.3.8.

We also recommend grabbing the latest version of toffeeserver which is also available on toffget.

docs.title: Desktop Environments
docs.text:
The Desktop Environment (DE) enabled by default in toffeeOS Developer Version 1.6.y and later is toffeeOS Desktop (packaged as toffeeos-desktop). toffeeOS Desktop and GNOME 40.y and 41.y are currently supported in 1.6.y and later DV releases.

In the final release of toffeeOS 1, we will give users the choice between the two user interfaces.

The DE by default in toffeeOS Developer Version 1.5 and earlier is GNOME 3.38 and 40.y. This is the only supported option for these earlier versions.

docs.title: Package Managers
docs.text: Package Managers are arguably one of the most fundamental parts of any distribution. Lucky for you, we've got two!

docs.title: toffget
docs.text:
toffget is our signature package manager, and where (most of) the fundamental packages for toffeeOS are maintained. These include: - security/authentication-related packages - packages for various features, including Android apps

You can check for updates to various packages by performing the following action in Console/Terminal apps:

sudo toffget fetch --all

To apply ("snag") any updates fetch receives:

sudo toffget snag-new -y

To purge a badly-behaving update from your system (only use the --rm-user-data flag if the package you're trying to remove stores its data in the /home folder):

sudo toffget purge (package-name) --rm-user-data -y

docs.title: RPM (DNF)
docs.text: We have removed support for RPM/DNF in toffeeOS Developer Version 2.0.

docs.title: Supported Email Standards
docs.text:
We're happy to support the most up-to-date standards for email security, fetching, and especially privacy. We require SSL be enabled on user's IMAP4/POP3/SMTP servers when sending or receiving email.

toffeeOS Developer Version supports the following: - mailboxes hosted on Hosted Exchange/Microsoft 365 for Business (as of toffeeOS Dev 1.6.4) - mailboxes hosted on Exchange Server 2016, 2019 - In protest of Microsoft moving Exchange Server to a subscription model (which we do not agree with), we will not be supporting Exchange Server 2022 at this time. Please use IMAP to interact with this release. - IMAP4 w/ SSL (recommended) - POP3 w/ SSL (not recommended) - SMTP w/ SSL

*in toffeeOS Developer Version 1.6.4, we began recommending IMAP4 (with SSL) connections to fetch mail from email servers. We may enforce the use of IMAP4 in future versions of toffeeOS Developer Version, including the final public release of toffeeOS 1.

docs.title: Syncfon
docs.text: Syncfon is an Experience app that is intended to bridge toffeeOS and chocolateOS devices together. It was introduced with toffeeOS Developer Version 1.5.

docs.title: Feature Set
docs.text:
• Syncfon shares your SMS and RCS conversations directly to the app, and includes push notifications, so you can stay in touch with the people you care about.
  • Syncfon allows you to send and receive SMS and RCS conversations to your heart's content!
  • Syncfon brings your notifications to the big (or small) screen. Get a notification on your phone? It will appear right on your desktop. And it works in reverse too. So you know which device it came from, it'll display its name right in the notification.
  • Syncfon allows you to screen share directly to your computer (we recommend an Intel processor from 2014 or later, or an AMD APU A8 and higher released in 2016 or later, or Ryzen 1000 or later) with direct inputs so you can use your device without needing to pick it up.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text: Select something from the dropdown!

docs.title: Default Mode
docs.text: Default Mode is the — as the name suggests — default user experience in toffeeOS Development Version. Unlike Enterprise and Education, it does not include their expanded features unless it is paired to a corresponding toffeeOS Developer Version instance using Server 1.5.1 and later.

docs.title: Education Mode
docs.text: toffeeOS Development Version 1.5.1 or later features an Education Mode for Educational institutions. This mode provides advanced features for schools, universities, and upper level institutions to tweak unicorn to their specific needs—whether that's more flexible permissions, time locks, or improved file sharing features for students and staff alike.

docs.title: How to Enable and Access Locally
docs.text: Education Mode must be enabled on an x86_64 (64-bit) build of toffeeOS Server Development Version 1.5.1 or later, and End Users (students, staff, administrators) must be signed into the same network that the unicorn Server is connected to, and signed into their Server Communicator app with their credentials.

docs.title: Remote Access
docs.text:
To enable Remote Access—a secure, remotely accessible bridge to your network resources for your students, staff, and administrators—simply tick the box in Settings and follow the steps to port forward your server's Bridging Port. The Bridging Port acts as a VPN tunnel for your End Users and allows them to access resources remotely that wouldn't be accessible otherwise.

Bridging Port is supported in toffeeOS Development Version 1.6 and later. The default port that administrators will need to port forward is 25101.

docs.title: Enterprise Mode
docs.text: toffeeOS Development Version 1.5.1 or later features an Enterprise mode meant for corporate environments. This mode provides advanced features for businesses (big and small) to tweak unicorn to their specific needs—whether that's more flexible permissions, time cards, or improved file sharing features for administrators and staff alike.

docs.title: How to Enable and Access Locally
docs.text: Enterprise Mode must be enabled on an x86_64 (64-bit) build of toffeeOS Server Development Version 1.5.1 or later, and End Users must be signed into the same network that the toffeeOS Server Development Version is connected to, and signed into their Server Communicator app with their credentials.

docs.title: Remote Access
docs.text: Added in Alpha with API level 200 (toffeeOS Development Version 2.0 and Development Server 2.0). Not officially sanctioned for use.

docs.title: x86 support deprecation
docs.text:
For the entire 3 years we've been building toffeeOS Developer Version, we've always included a 32-bit (x86) of the operating system for compatibility purposes. Our goal was to support as many systems as feasibly possible - and we did. While we are certainly proud of this, we realized it significantly impacts our development time and resiliency to resolve bugs on two incredibly different codebases.

x86-only systems are becoming more and more rare as time goes on. So we're getting rid of the added stress (and ultimately, "busy work"): with toffeeOS Developer Version 1.5, we have deprecated support for the x86 builds. And once toffeeOS Developer Version 1.8 is rolled to the Stable ring (taking 1.7's place), x86 builds will no longer be supported.

We realize this change is difficult. But x86 systems are unpopular now and 64-bit (x86_64) is the way to go for any software release.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Q: Will 32-bit app support go away? A: No, 32-bit apps will continue to be supported for backwards compatibility reasons, even after this change.

Q: Will there be security updates pushed out after it is deprecated? A: Yes, we'll continue pushing out features updates until toffeeOS Developer Version 1.7, after which point, only security/performance/stability updates will be rolled out. x86 systems will not get toffeeOS Developer Version 1.9.

Q: Why did you extend the 32-bit deprecation date A: As requested by testers, it gives us (and them) a bit more buffer room to upgrade systems, and refine other branches of development to make even more changes before pulling the plug. Feature updates and compatibility, however, will be limited.

docs.text:
(could be subject to change at any time!)
